While, as previously stated, this book might be a good beginning point for a person starting their journey as a caregiver, I would ask the newcomers to this role please do not feel guilty if you are not engaging in everything contained in this book; you are no doubt doing an excellent job, and the very best you can.

yorum: I got this because of my internal suffering that I was trying to understand, I resonated with the title itself. The book is very well written. I enjoyed the format. There is knowledge to be read here and I believe the author had good intentions of wanting to help others. But. This book kind of exemplifies how black and white (extremes) thinking is sensational to our human brain. This good, this bad. Which is dangerous for those like me who lean on this type of negative thought pattern, to make sense of daily life. My problem mainly is the Emphasis on "either or" of being an Externalist or an Internalist. I appreciate the creativity, however everyone has regulation skills that are on a spectrum. You are not an internalizer. You could definitely be a person who usually internally regulated. That does not mean you don't externally regulate. I think an example might be when you seek reassurance or encouragement from those around you. If you had immature parents, you likely had to internalize to survive, so you never felt safe to seek external regulation from "safe" individuals. The problem is putting an identity tag on a method of regulation when you definitely have both styles. It's not possible to live in society, among other humans, and not learn both styles. I'd say if you read this book and you're like me, please don't lean too much into the labels. My mom was immature but she also loved me in her own way. Being a parent doesn't come with an instruction manual. It's sad to be neglected and it's tragic to receive abuse from your protectors, that really changes you. But you can't heal without empathy and compassion. Learn to empathize the best you can, while also practicing enough self compassion to forgive yourself, for the chaotic choices made throughout life that led you to buying these types of books. We didn't design our nervous system, it's not going to heal after one book. Healing your damaged nervous system from childhood is a long process that requires deep and consistent inner reflection, while honoring that you deserve to feel safe around others. Especially those that care about you, those that aren't abusing you or neglecting you like your parents possibly did.
